elements.element: Customer is not obligated to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: PB remains obligated to make fixed payments upon specified terminations, and Section 14.4.2 expressly provides that those payments are “in lieu of any claim for damages” by SFJ.

elements.element: Customer is not obligated to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: The redline removes the 300% multiple and 25% annual interest uplift. The remaining termination payments are based on Development Costs actually paid or incurred, with no express punitive multiple, premium, or penalty.

elements.element: Any liquidated-payment obligation of Customer is triggered only by early termination.
elements.evidence: The relevant payment obligations arise only “[i]n the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement” under the specified termination provisions.

elements.element: The early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No three-month-fee cap is included. The amounts are instead calculated by reference to 100% of Development Costs or Development Costs plus potentially continuing Approval Payments.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer in connection with the termination.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4.2 states that the applicable Section 14.2 payment is “in lieu of any claim for damages” SFJ may have arising from the circumstances forming the basis of the termination.

result.reason: The redline removes the most punitive features but retains fixed termination payments expressly operating in lieu of damages, so the preferred position is not achieved. It also fails the fallback because no three-month-fee cap is stated. Although the changes are limited to the relevant payment formulas and preserve unrelated commercial terms, they do not reach either complete position.
